  City Council Minutes

  City Hall Council Chamber

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmember Madison)

CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:01 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding significant exposure to potential litigation pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): One potential case

  CONFERENCE with Labor Negotiator pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54957.6
  Employee Title and Unrepresented Employee: City Manager

  The above closed session items were discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time.

  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): Two potential cases

  The first case for the Closed Session Item above was discussed,
  with no reportable action at this time. The second case was not
  discussed.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:49
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Hampton.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  CouncilmemberTyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon

Council Minutes  1  09/29/2025
   Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

n  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  Chief Assistant City Attorney Arnold Lee
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS City Clerk Jomsky administered the oath of office to Jessica
  Richards, City nominee to the Urban Forestry Advisory Committee.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the month of
  October 2025 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month
  in Pasadena, which recognizes the various accomplishments and
  contributions of those with disabilities throughout the community.
  Valerie Struski, Vice Chair of the City's Accessibility and Disability
  Commission, and Chris Otero, President of Pasadena Civitan Club,
  accepted the proclamation, thanked the City Council for this
  recognition, and introduced Michaela Sanchez, Civitan Club Event
  Chair, who announced details of Civitan's upcoming event at Villa
  Esperanza on October 23, 2025.

  Mayor Gordo presented certificates of achievement to the Pasadena
  Senior Women's Basketball League for winning a bronze medal at
  the 2025 National Senior Games. Sarah Letts, member of the
f  Pasadena Senior Women's Basketball League, thanked the City
  Council for the recognition and City staff for their support.

  Mayor Gordo announced that the City received the 2025 California
  Stormwater Quality Association Award for its Stormwater Master
  Plan and Program. Karen Cowan, Executive Director of California
  Stormwater Quality Association, presented the award to Greg de
  Vinck, Public Works Director, Brent Maue, City Engineer, and Dawn
  Petschauer, emphasizing the importance of protecting the aquafer
  system and collecting water for the future.

 RECOMMENDATIONS  REQUEST BY COUNCILMEMBER MADISON FOR AN UPDATE
FROM OFFICERS AND  ON PROGRESS MADE IN ESTABLISHING SISTER CITY
DEPARTMENTS  RELATIONSHIPS WITH CITIES IN MEXICO, INCLUDING
  GUANAJUATO, MEXICO
City Council
  Councilmember Madison provided introductory remarks on the item,
  noting that he asked for the item to be agendized to discuss the
  Pasadena Sister Cities Committee's process for establishing a sister
  city relationship with a city in Latin America, hie advocated for the
  City Council to accept the invitation from the City of Guanajuato,
  Mexico, to attend and celebrate the Dia de los Muertos (Day of the
  Dead) event in Guanajuato at the end of October. He also expressed
  concerns regarding the recent changes to the Committee's bylaws
  and membership protocols.

  Mayor Gordo stated that the process for establishing a new sister
  city relationship requires following the protocols established by the
  Pasadena Sister Cities Committee, as well as following the City's
  own rules and process in that regard, which first requires the
  Pasadena Sister Cities Committee to submit its recommendation to
  the City Council, noting that such an action has not occurred.

  Discussion ensued regarding the introduction of a delegation and the
  extension of an invitation from the Municipal President of Guanajuato
  to visit the city.

  Councilmember Hampton suggested that the Pasadena Sister Cities
  Committee President, Lena Louise Kennedy, provide information
  and explain the process for establishing a sister city.

  Lena Louise Kennedy, President of the Pasadena Sister Cities
  Committee, submitted the Pasadena Sister Cities Committee, Inc.,
  Board Handbook, Operating Policies and Procedures, and voiced
  strong concerns regarding the agendized request. She spoke on the
  history of her involvement and serving on the Committee, expressed
  concerns regarding the work done to initiate a sister city relationship
  with Guanajuato, referring back to the handbook and noting that
  requested action does not follow established protocols or
  procedures, and is inconsistent with past City practices. She also
  referred to Committee's adopted bylaws and reported on the work
  done by the Pasadena Sister Cities Committee, and urged
  community members and the City Council to work cooperatively and
  together to establish sister city relationships in the future in
  accordance with the Committee's nonprofit bylaws and the City
  Council's protocols.

  Mayor Gordo submitted material related to the matter, including
  guidelines of Sister City International (SCI), describing the process
  for establishing a sister city relationship, as well as email
  communications describing events that have taken place to date in

Council Minutes  10  09/29/2025
   relation to efforts made to explore potential sister city opportunities
  in Mexico, including Guanajuato. He noted that an essential step in

n  the process includes having the highest ranking elected official of the
  jurisdiction to approve and formalize such a partnership, which has
  not occurred.

  Councilmember Cole expressed his concerns regarding the tone of
  the discussion, made a motion to table the matter and refer this issue
  back to the Pasadena Sister Cities Committee, and to follow the
  established process.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for the City Council not to take
  any action on the item, and to allow the Pasadena Sister Cities
  Committee to continue forward with their process and to return to the
  City Council if and when action needs to be taken.

  Councilmember Madison submitted letters from the Pasadena Sister
  Cities Committee and the Municipal President of Guanajuato,
  indicating interest in exploring a sister city relationship between
  Pasadena and Guanajuato, Mexico, as well as other materials,
  including a report and recommendation from Pasadena Sister Cities
  Ad-Hoc Committee to pursue such a relationship, noting an invitation
  from the Guanajuato City Council to Pasadena to visit the City of
  Guanajuato.

  The following individuals strongly advocated on following the
